citations.quote: **EGFR**: Exon 19 deletion (p.E746_A750del) detected by targeted PCR/NGS assay.
**EGFR mutation analysis (PCR):** No sensitizing mutations detected.

candidates.description: Presence of a sensitizing EGFR mutation in the lung tumor.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify 'EGFR' in molecular testing sections. Label as positive if a mutation (e.g., exon 19 deletion) is 'detected'; label as negative if 'No sensitizing mutations detected' is explicitly stated.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if a sensitizing EGFR mutation is detected by PCR or NGS; negative if no sensitizing mutations are detected or if specifically described as wild-type. Absence of documentation is not a negative result.
candidates.name: EGFR Mutation Status
candidates.uncertainty: Whether all non-sensitizing variants are grouped under 'negative' or if they should be treated as missing.

candidates.description: The percentage of viable tumor cells showing partial or complete membranous staining for PD-L1.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Locate the 'PD-L1' entry in the Immunohistochemistry (IHC) table and extract the associated numeric percentage.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numeric percentage (%) of tumor cells staining positive for PD-L1 as reported by the Tumor Proportion Score (TPS).
candidates.name: PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: Whether different PD-L1 clones (e.g., 22C3) are interchangeable for this variable.

limitations: Small cohort of patients represented in the provided excerpts.
Variable NGS panel sizes (324-gene vs 500-gene) across different patients.
Variability in reporting of EGFR status (some reports use IHC, others use PCR/NGS).
summary: The evidence identifies baseline clinical and molecular characteristics of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) patients, specifically focusing on histological subtypes (adenocarcinoma, large-cell carcinoma), molecular drivers (EGFR mutations), and immune markers (PD-L1 expression).
